Chapter II · The Sovereign Drape मातृरूपेण संस्थिता Kora Mulberry & Sindoor Zari

Maa

✦

The Maternal Sanctum The mother. The creator. The quiet crimson dawn before the dhak awakens the courtyard—draped in unbleached kora mulberry silk and temple gold.

01 · Sacred Iconography

The Filigree Mukut & Solar Prabhamandala

Inspired by traditional Bengali dak-er-saaj and antique gold temple crowns, the radial lotus halo echoes the geometric chakras woven into our Banarasi pallu medallions.

Durga.

The Living Force Courage woven in pure twisted zari. Grace that flows through six yards of living crimson and ivory—honoring the sovereign radiance within every woman.

Chapter III · Sandhya Aarti & Courtyard Rhythm

In her light, we celebrate.

When twilight settles over the sandstone arches and a hundred marigolds ring the brass lamps, silk becomes movement—answering the cadence of the festive courtyard.

Duality in Motion · Saptami Twilight

The Dialogue of Sindoor Crimson & Peacock Emerald

Two complementary loom traditions—Varanasi kadwa brocade in vermilion-red and Kanchipuram three-shuttle korvai in peacock-emerald—woven to catch candlelight in mid-twirl.

Illuminate the Courtyard Mandala

Tap any brass lamp below to kindle the Sandhya Aarti ring (5 of 7 lamps lit).

Chapter IV · Tantrokta Devi Suktam & The Golden Loom

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु शक्तिरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥

Yā Devī Sarvabhūteṣu Śaktirūpeṇa Saṃsthitā · Namastasyai Namastasyai Namastasyai Namo Namaḥ

“To the Divine Goddess who abides in all beings as Sovereign Strength—to Her we bow in reverence, again and again.”

✦ Weave Resonance: Handwoven Kadwa Lotus-Mandala Zari Brocade — 100-count Katan warp with electroplated silver-gold kalabattu threads.

Chapter V · Architecture of the Sacred Drape

WOVEN IN DIVINITY.

GARBHAGRIHA EDITION ✦ ANVAYA ARCHIVE ✦ HANDLOOM SILK & ZARI
01 · The Patience of the Loom

The Loom of Silence

Before a single gold motif catches the festival lamps, two master weavers sit in quiet synchrony—passing each extra-weft bobbin by hand across thousands of silk warp threads.

02 · Botanical & Temple Grammar

Mallika & Konika Motifs

Inspired by fresh jasmine gajra garlands and carved temple pillars, the border interlaces floral बेल (bel) creepers with protective kumbha temple spires.

03 · Tactile Heirloom Weight

Six Yards of Devotion

Designed not for a single season, but as an heirloom vessel of memory—holding the scent of dhuno resin, sandalwood, and autumn shiuli blossoms across generations.

04 · Interactive Lookbook

Study the Weave

Examine the warp, weft, and motif symbolism of this monochrome heirloom study inside the interactive lookbook modal.

Chapter VI · Curated Exhibition

The Pujo Anthology

Six devotional silk studies conceived for the sacred hours of Sharadiya Durga Puja—from the quiet conch of Mahalaya dawn to the vermilion joy of Dashami Sindoor Khela. Select any edition to inspect its imagined weave anatomy and lighting response. All materials, loom details and ritual pairings below are fictional design specifications, not verified products or provenance.

I · Mahalaya & Dashami
Korial Banarasi · Unbleached Kora Mulberry

Aparajita — The Unconquered

Sunlit kora ivory field framed by a deep alta-crimson korial border and temple-spire (kumbha) antique gold zari pallu.

Motif: Kumbha & Shiuli
II · Mahashtami Pushpanjali
Kadwa Banarasi · Sanctum Maroon Katan

Rudrakshi — Sanctum Flame

Deep garbhagriha maroon katan silk strewn with hand-turned kadwa lotus medallions in burnished copper-gold kalabattu.

Motif: Sahasrara Padma
III · Saptami Courtyard
Three-Shuttle Korvai · Peacock Mulberry

Mayurakshi — Twilight Courtyard

Iridescent peacock-teal warp interwoven with emerald weft, anchored by a bold burnished-gold temple gopuram border.

Motif: Mayura & Gopuram
IV · Sandhi Puja 108 Diyas
Katan Zari Tissue · Molten Amber & Gold

Kanakambari — 108 Lamps

Luminous pure golden tissue weave that mirrors the sacred cusp of Ashtami and Nabami when 108 earthen lamps ignite simultaneously.

Motif: Ashtadala Kamal
V · Mahanabami Aarti
Butidar Jangla Brocade · Sindoor Crimson

Simhavahini — Sovereign Vermilion

Vivid vermilion-red mulberry silk pleated with dense metallic gold tissue borders and kalga-bel floral scrolls across the anchal.

Motif: Kalga & Shankha
VI · Vijaya Evening
Ganga-Jamuna Brocade · Silver & Antique Gold

Chandrachuda — Vijaya Dusk

Contemplative silver-and-gold Ganga-Jamuna zari work pairing cool moonlight silver threads with warm temple gold borders.

Motif: Mallika & Konika

The Philosophy of Anvaya

Some stories are not written.
They are woven.

In Sanskrit, Anvaya (अन्वय) signifies lineage, continuity, and the natural connection between sacred word and meaning. Conceived as a digital homage to India’s master handloom clusters, every section of this concept study celebrates the union of Shakti iconography and slow textile craft.

Chapter VII · Sacred Benediction

नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥

“Salutations again and again to the Divine Mother—whose radiance lives in every home, every lamp, and every woven thread.”
